builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Looped Models are Fast Multi-Token Predictors
summary: Floodgates replaces separate draft-model speculative decoding with a self-speculative scheme: a block of mask tokens is appended as a suffix and a LoRA-adapted shallow-loop drafter predicts multiple future tokens in parallel, verified by the deep loops. The cost is a training stage (low-rank adaptation on the looped model), the requirement of an all-depth-trained looped architecture, and the added serving complexity of mask-suffix drafting and verification. It can fail if the deployed model is not a looped model trained at all depths, since the reported speedup depends on the shallow drafter conditioning on the deep prefix cache, and the 7.5x figure is a best-case bound across benchmarks rather than a guaranteed workload result.
rationale: The method requires an existing looped language model and a low-rank adaptation training pass, so it is only actionable if the reader already deploys looped models; otherwise it offers no path for standard architectures.
technique: Self-speculative mask-suffix drafting in looped models

claims.statement: Floodgates replaces separate draft-model speculative decoding with a self-speculative scheme: a block of mask tokens is appended as a suffix and a LoRA-adapted shallow-loop drafter predicts multiple future tokens in parallel, verified by the deep loops. The cost is a training stage (low-rank adaptation on the looped model), the requirement of an all-depth-trained looped architecture, and the added serving complexity of mask-suffix drafting and verification. It can fail if the deployed model is not a looped model trained at all depths, since the reported speedup depends on the shallow drafter conditioning on the deep prefix cache, and the 7.5x figure is a best-case bound across benchmarks rather than a guaranteed workload result.

Up to 7.5x inference acceleration over baseline decoding, reported as the fastest lossless method in most settings across seven models, five benchmarks, varied batch sizes, and greedy and sampled decoding.
